answer.generated: Dynamic scheduling in the context of overcoming data hazards reorders instructions to reduce stalls caused by output dependences and antidependences. Output dependences occur when an instruction depends on the result of a previous instruction, while antidependences arise when a later instruction depends on the result of a previous instruction before it has been written. By dynamically scheduling instructions, the processor can exploit these dependencies to reorder operations, thereby avoiding stalls. For instance, in the given assembly code, if instruction 2 has an output dependence on a previous instruction and instruction 3 has an antidependence on the result of instruction 2, dynamic scheduling could reorder these instructions to first execute the operation producing the result needed by both, thus eliminating the stall.
